persona.role: immigration lawyer at a small firm

sent_to_model:
I want to put a short proposal in our shared planning doc before Marcus and I sit down on Thursday to plan the cap season. The ask: we move our internal deadline for H-1B registration intake up to January 15 instead of letting employers trickle in through February. Marcus is generally fine with change but he hates anything that sounds like we're scolding clients, so it needs to make the case on workload and risk, not blame. Rosa should be able to read it too. Last season's numbers are below. Please draft it as a doc section, headed, a few paragraphs, maybe a short list of what would actually change. Include the steps below and Rosa’s six weeks to chase gaps.

- last season (March 2026) we filed 14 registrations for 6 employer clients; 9 of the 14 came in during the final week of February
- Rosa logged roughly 11 hours of overtime the week the window opened
- intake now = we email the questionnaire whenever the employer asks; no set date
- proposed: engagement letters + one-page questionnaire go out the week of Dec 7, intake closes January 15, anything later handled case by case
- registration fee is $215 per beneficiary, employers already budget for it in Q1
- Brightwater Analytics sent a beneficiary's passport scan two days before the window; it had expired in October, we only caught it because Rosa checked the dates
- one HR contact told me she'd have happily sent everything in January if we'd asked
- most of the crunch is our process, not client delay; nobody gave them a date
- an earlier date protects us too, the registration itself is simple but errors are expensive (wrong passport = invalid selection)
- January 15 is realistic, HR teams are back from holidays and have budgets set
- Marcus agrees on Thursday so we can send the December letters
- frame it as better service, not as clients being late
- Rosa owns the tracker; mention she gets a clean six weeks to chase gaps

(About me: immigration lawyer at a small firm, 45, Chicago, Illinois. Length: it should come to roughly 250-400 words.)

must_cover: Proposes January 15 intake closure and explains workload and risk reasons.
Schedules engagement letters and the one-page questionnaire for the week of December 7 and handles later intake case by case.
Gives Rosa the tracker and six weeks to chase gaps.
Seeks Marcus’s agreement on Thursday so the December letters can go out.
